title: Friday evening on production
text:
It was Friday, 6 p.m., and I was ready to go home. Then my phone started to ring. The monitoring system sent an alert: the website was very slow, and many users could not log in.

We joined a call. Dan, the senior engineer, asked a simple question: "What changed today?" We checked the list of releases. One deployment went out at 5:30. It had a small change in the database query. On my laptop it worked perfectly, but with real data it was much slower.

Nobody blamed anyone. Dan said we needed to fix the problem first and talk about the reasons later. We decided to roll back the release. It took only four minutes, and the graphs slowly went back to normal.

After that, we wrote a short report. We also added a rule: no big deployments on Friday afternoon. I got home at 8 p.m., tired but happy. I learned that a good team is calm when something breaks.

questions.prompt: What was the cause of the problem?
options: A small change in a database query
A mistake in the monitoring system
Too many users in the evening
questions.explanation: Реліз о 5:30 містив зміну в запиті до бази даних, яка на реальних даних працювала значно повільніше.

questions.prompt: How did the team solve the problem?
questions.explanation: Команда відкотила реліз, і графіки повернулися до норми.

questions.prompt: What is the author's main conclusion?
options: Friday is the best day for releases.
A good team stays calm when something goes wrong.
questions.explanation: В останньому реченні автор каже, що добра команда залишається спокійною, коли щось ламається.
